mainEntity.name: When is it necessary to repair knockdown texture instead of painting over it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Knockdown texture should be repaired whenever you notice cracks, peeling, water stains, or holes from drywall anchors or plumbing cutouts. If the drywall beneath has softened from a leak, the damaged drywall must be cut out and replaced before texturing can occur. Hairline cracks often point to minor house settling or joint tape failure, which requires re-taping and mudding before applying the texture coat. Delaying repairs can allow peeling edges to catch and pull away larger texture sections.
acceptedAnswer.description: Repair is necessary when there are gouges, holes, water damage, or peeling compound. Painting over bare or damaged spots highlights the missing texture rather than hiding it.
